b: With Sales Hub and LinkedIn Sales Navigator, sales reps can schedule InMail and connection request tasks alongside email and other follow-up activities. HubSpot manages the sequence timing and task reminders, while reps review prospect information and complete LinkedIn interactions themselves.

In this guide, LinkedIn automation means adding task reminders to a structured HubSpot sales sequence — not using bots to automatically send LinkedIn messages or connection requests. This approach combines the consistency of sales automation with the context available through CRM automation, helping teams organize outreach without automatically sending LinkedIn messages.

LinkedIn automation broadly refers to using workflows to organize or perform social selling activities on the platform. In HubSpot, it means using sequences to schedule manual tasks for LinkedIn InMail and connection requests. HubSpot creates the reminders, but a sales rep must complete each LinkedIn action.

LinkedIn Sales Navigator is LinkedIn’s sales prospecting platform. HubSpot’s LinkedIn Sales Navigator integration lets eligible users view LinkedIn profile details, shared connections, and relevant account information alongside HubSpot contact and company records.
According to HubSpot’s 2026 State of Sales report, 48% of sales professionals say buyers expect more personalized experiences from sales teams.
In my experience, the best LinkedIn follow-ups still depend on a rep noticing something relevant and turning that context into a genuinely useful interaction.
Why Sales Teams Automate LinkedIn Tasks

Sales teams automate LinkedIn task reminders to keep outreach consistent, timely, and organized alongside emails and calls. A sequence can remind a rep to research a prospect, send a connection request, or follow up with an InMail. Reps still decide whether each interaction is appropriate and complete the action themselves. Connecting LinkedIn Sales Navigator with HubSpot also gives reps access to prospect and company information alongside their CRM records, helping them prepare more relevant outreach.

Within Sales Hub, sales automation tools let teams build sequences that combine automated emails with manual task reminders. This helps teams coordinate their sales stack, without managing every follow-up in a separate tool. Unlike broader workflow automation, a LinkedIn sequence task reminds a rep to take an action rather than automatically sending the LinkedIn message.
How to Add LinkedIn Task Steps to a HubSpot Sequence

To add LinkedIn tasks to a HubSpot sequence, first connect LinkedIn Sales Navigator to HubSpot. Then create a sequence in Sales Hub and add InMail or connection request tasks at the appropriate points in the cadence. These tasks remind reps to complete LinkedIn activities manually.
Connect LinkedIn Sales Navigator to HubSpot.

To use the LinkedIn Sales Navigator integration, each user needs an assigned Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise seat and a LinkedIn Sales Navigator Advanced Plus plan. The Sales Navigator Advanced plan alone does not meet HubSpot’s documented integration requirements.
In HubSpot, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar and select HubSpot Marketplace.
Search for LinkedIn Sales Navigator and select the app.

Each user must install the LinkedIn Sales Navigator app while signed in to HubSpot with their own login. Once connected, reps can view relevant Sales Navigator information alongside their HubSpot CRM records.
The standard LinkedIn Sales Navigator integration does not support importing contacts from LinkedIn into HubSpot.
To view LinkedIn Sales Navigator information in HubSpot:
Navigate to CRM > Contacts or CRM > Companies and open the relevant record.

Find the LinkedIn Sales Navigator card in the right sidebar. If the app was installed after October 7, 2025, a Super Admin or user with permission to customize record layouts must add the card to the sidebar.

On contact records, review details such as the person’s job title, company, time in their current role, location, and industry. Click View more to access additional Sales Navigator information, including shared connections, interests, and recent activity.
On company records, review information such as industry, size, and location. Additional Sales Navigator views can provide company news and information about relevant people at the account.

You can also send an InMail manually from a HubSpot contact or company record. Click Send InMail in the Sales Navigator card, compose your message in the LinkedIn pop-up box, and click Send. The conversation will not automatically be saved to the record’s activity timeline, although you can manually log the interaction.
For more details, see HubSpot’s LinkedIn Sales Navigator setup guide.

An InMail task in a HubSpot sequence reminds a sales rep to send a LinkedIn InMail at a scheduled point in the outreach process. The sequence creates the task reminder, but the rep must write and send the message manually. You can add these reminders alongside automated emails and call tasks in HubSpot sequences.
In HubSpot, navigate to Sales > Sequences.
Click Create Sequence. Choose Start from scratch or select a pre-made sequence template, then click Create sequence.
In the sequence editor, click the pencil icon to name your sequence.
Click the + icon to add a step.
In the right panel, select Sales Navigator - InMail task.
Under Task details, choose whether to pause the sequence until the task is completed. Enter a task title, set its priority, and select a task queue.
Use the Notes field to add relevant context or draft the message you want the rep to send. Text entered here will not automatically populate in the LinkedIn Sales Navigator message box.
Click Add. Continue adding sequence steps as needed, then click Save.
When the rep completes the task from a queue, LinkedIn Sales Navigator opens on the contact’s HubSpot record. The rep can then compose and send the InMail manually.

InMail tasks are useful when a LinkedIn message serves a specific purpose within a broader outreach cadence. For example, a rep might follow up with someone whose recent company activity makes the timing relevant, continue a conversation from another channel, or introduce themselves to a prospect after researching the account.

Pro tip: Add the core message or key talking points to the task’s Notes field. They won’t automatically appear in the LinkedIn composer, but they give the rep a useful starting point when the reminder comes due.

A connection request task reminds a sales rep to send a LinkedIn connection request at the appropriate point in a HubSpot sequence. As with InMail tasks, HubSpot schedules the reminder while the rep completes the LinkedIn action manually.
To add a connection request task:
Open your sequence in the HubSpot sequence editor.
Click the + icon where you want the connection request to appear.
In the right panel, select Sales Navigator - Connection request task.
Under Task details, enter a task title and priority, choose whether the sequence should pause until the task is completed, and select a task queue.
In the Notes field, add a reminder about why you want to connect or include the message you plan to send. The message will not automatically populate in LinkedIn Sales Navigator.
Click Add, then save your sequence when you’ve finished adding steps.
When completing the task from a queue, the rep can use LinkedIn Sales Navigator on the contact’s record to review the prospect and send the connection request.

Connection request tasks work best when there is a clear reason to establish a professional relationship. For example, a rep might connect with someone they met at an event, identify a relevant contact at a target account, or follow up after an earlier exchange through another channel.
Because the request is manual, the rep can review the prospect’s profile and adapt the message before sending it.
When to Use LinkedIn Tasks vs. Email vs. Calls

Use LinkedIn tasks, email, and calls based on the purpose of each interaction. LinkedIn is useful for establishing professional connections and targeted outreach. Email works well for detailed communication, and calls support conversations that benefit from an immediate exchange. The best approach depends on the prospect and context, not on following the same multichannel checklist for everyone.

A sequence can combine these channels without requiring every prospect to receive every type of outreach. If your next step is an email, follow-up email automation may help you manage that communication. LinkedIn-specific sequence tasks still require a rep to complete the action manually.
How to Personalize LinkedIn Follow-Up With CRM Context

To personalize LinkedIn follow-up, review the prospect’s contact details, company information, and previous sales activity in HubSpot before completing the LinkedIn task. Use that context to identify a relevant reason to reach out and tailor the message to the person, rather than relying on a generic template.

Start with the contact record. Review the person’s role, company, and previous interactions with your team. The LinkedIn Sales Navigator integration provides additional information. For example, the tools Icebreaker view lets you find shared connections, experiences, interests, and a link to the contact’s recent activity.

Next, review the company record. Look for relevant details about the account, including its industry, size, and location. Sales Navigator’s company views can also provide news and information about people at a company. Those updates may help you understand whether there’s a timely reason to reach out.

Finally, check the contact’s activity history in HubSpot. Review previous emails, calls, and other recorded interactions before writing your LinkedIn message. Keep in mind that InMail conversations aren’t automatically saved to the HubSpot record through the standard Sales Navigator integration, so you may need to log those interactions manually.

Pro tip: Instead of creating generic tasks that say “Send LinkedIn message,” add a useful prompt for the rep. For example: “Review the prospect’s recent company announcement and write a connection request that references something relevant from it.” This gives the rep a reason to personalize the outreach without prescribing the exact message.
